A circuit comprises an array of programmable memory elements fabricated on a substrate, each memory element having one or more processable regions which, when processed by an external process in which a material is applied to at least partially cover one or more of the regions, are configured to program that memory element to one of multiple states;a first set of control lines connected to the array of memory elements, by which the contents of each individual memory element are capable of being accessed by control signals applied to a respective combination of at least two control lines in the first set of control lines;and an array of second circuit elements, different to the memory elements, each connected to a control line of the first set of control lines and to another control line of a second set of control lines, different to the first set of control lines, so as to provide access to second circuit elements in the array.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: A circuit comprises

outputs.L1: A circuit comprises: an array of programmable memory elements fabricated on a substrate, each memory element having one or more processable regions that, when processed by an external process in which a material is applied to at least partially cover one or more of the regions, are configured to program the memory element to one of multiple states; a first set of control lines connected to the array of memory elements, through which the contents of each individual memory element are capable of being accessed by control signals applied to a respective combination of at least two control lines in the first set; and an array of second circuit elements, distinct from the memory elements, each connected to a control line of the first set and to another control line of a second set of control lines, the second set being distinct from the first set, thereby providing access to the second circuit elements in the array.
outputs.L2: A circuit includes an array of programmable memory elements formed on a substrate. Each memory element contains one or more regions configured for processing by an external operation that applies a material so as to cover at least part of one or more such regions, thereby setting the memory element to one of several possible states. A first group of control lines is coupled to the memory-element array, enabling the contents of each individual memory element to be accessed through control signals supplied to a corresponding combination of at least two control lines from that first group. The circuit further includes an array of second circuit elements that are distinct from the memory elements. Each second circuit element is coupled both to a control line in the first group and to another control line in a separate, second group of control lines, thereby permitting access to the second circuit elements within the array.
outputs.L3:
The circuit comprises an array of programmable memory elements fabricated on a substrate. Each memory element includes one or more regions that can be selectively programmed into multiple states by externally applying a material so that it covers at least a portion of those regions.

A first set of control lines is connected to the memory array. Individual memory elements are selectively accessed by applying control signals to a designated combination of at least two control lines within this first set.

The circuit further includes an array of second circuit elements that are distinct from the programmable memory elements. These second circuit elements are accessible through connections to both the first set of control lines and a separate, second set of control lines.
outputs.L4:
A programmable integrated circuit includes an array of memory elements that can be set to any of multiple states after fabrication. Each memory element has a region covered by material that can be processed from outside the circuit, for example by selectively adding, removing, or altering the material with optical, thermal, electrical, or mechanical energy. Processing a selected region changes an electrical characteristic of the corresponding memory element—such as its resistance, capacitance, conductivity, or connection state—thereby storing a desired value. Individual memory elements are selected through respective combinations of at least two control lines belonging to a first set, allowing the elements to be addressed without requiring a dedicated control line for every element.

The circuit further includes a separate array of functional circuit elements. Each of these elements is coupled to one or more control lines from the first set and to one or more control lines from a distinct second set. A particular circuit element can therefore be selected or operated by activating an appropriate combination of shared control lines from the two sets. The first-set lines may be reused for both programming or reading the memory array and controlling the additional circuit array, while the second-set lines provide further selection, routing, or operating capability.

This shared-line architecture reduces the number of conductors, terminals, drivers, and addressing components needed on the integrated circuit. At the same time, the externally processable regions permit configuration of the memory elements into multiple programmed states, and the additional circuit-element array extends the device’s functionality. Depending on the implementation, the circuit elements may perform switching, logic, sensing, routing, signal processing, or other operations governed by the programmed memory states and the selected control-line combinations.
outputs.L5: A circuit comprises a collection of electrical components connected to form a closed path through which electric current can flow. Typical components include a power source, wires, switches, resistors, capacitors, and loads such as lamps or motors. When the circuit is closed, the power source supplies energy and current moves through the connected components. If the path is broken, the circuit is open and current stops flowing. Circuits may be arranged in series, where components share one path, or in parallel, where current can travel through multiple branches.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style independent claim for a circuit containing externally programmable memory elements and a separately addressable array of other circuit elements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in one formal patent claim, a substrate-based memory array whose elements are programmed by applying material to selected regions, where first control lines access the memory and a second set of lines helps access different circuit elements.
counterfactuals.output: 1. A memory device comprising: a substrate; a plurality of memory elements disposed in an array on the substrate, each memory element including a respective programmable region configured to assume a programmed state by selective application of a material to the respective programmable region; a first plurality of control lines coupled to the plurality of memory elements and configured to selectively access the memory elements; a plurality of circuit elements associated with the array; and a second plurality of lines coupled to the plurality of circuit elements and configured, in cooperation with at least one of the first plurality of control lines, to selectively access different circuit elements of the plurality of circuit elements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a broad apparatus claim covering an array of programmable memory cells, row/column control-line addressing, and an additional array of non-memory components connected across two distinct control-line sets.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Formulate a single patent claim for a circuit in which each memory element can assume multiple states after an external material-deposition process, individual memory elements are accessed through combinations of at least two control lines, and secondary circuit elements are also addressable.
counterfactuals.output: 1. A circuit comprising: a plurality of control lines; a plurality of memory elements, each memory element being individually addressable by a respective combination of at least two of the control lines and being configured, following an externally performed material-deposition process, to assume any one of three or more distinguishable memory states; and a plurality of secondary circuit elements distinct from the memory elements, each secondary circuit element being addressable through a respective combination of the control lines.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate claim language for an integrated circuit comprising process-programmable memory regions on a substrate, a first control-line network for selecting individual memories, and a distinct array of secondary elements coupled to both the first network and a second control-line network.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **An integrated circuit comprising:**

a substrate;

a plurality of process-programmable memory regions disposed on the substrate, each process-programmable memory region having a programmed state established by at least one fabrication process;

a first control-line network coupled to the plurality of process-programmable memory regions and configured to select an individual process-programmable memory region from among the plurality of process-programmable memory regions;

a second control-line network distinct from the first control-line network; and

an array of secondary elements, separate from the plurality of process-programmable memory regions, each secondary element being coupled to at least one control line of the first control-line network and at least one control line of the second control-line network.

2. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein the first control-line network comprises a plurality of intersecting selection lines, and each process-programmable memory region is selectable according to a combination of signals applied to respective selection lines.

3. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein the programmed state of each process-programmable memory region is defined by a presence, absence, or physical configuration of a conductive path formed during fabrication of the integrated circuit.

4. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein the second control-line network is configured to select a subset of the secondary elements independently of selection of the process-programmable memory regions.

5. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein each secondary element is addressable according to a first signal conveyed by the first control-line network and a second signal conveyed by the second control-line network.

6. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein the secondary elements comprise switching elements, logic elements, sensing elements, storage elements, or combinations thereof.

7. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein at least a portion of the first control-line network is shared between selection of the process-programmable memory regions and operation of the array of secondary elements.

8. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, further comprising control circuitry configured to apply a first set of control signals to the first control-line network to access a selected process-programmable memory region and to apply a second set of control signals to the first and second control-line networks to access a selected secondary element.

9. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein the plurality of process-programmable memory regions and the array of secondary elements occupy laterally distinct portions of the substrate.

10. **The integrated circuit of claim 1**, wherein the array of secondary elements is arranged in rows and columns, the first control-line network being coupled to the rows and the second control-line network being coupled to the columns.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
